# Preserve reviewed resume edits

## What & Why
The local resume intake correctly keeps extracted values in a review panel, but the acceptance path does not consistently use the reviewer’s edited proposal value when saving structured profile data. Contact location proposals can also be accepted without applying their city and region fields. Fix this so the review-first promise is truthful: accepted and edited values become the saved profile, while rejected proposals remain out of the profile.

## Done looks like
- Editing and accepting a contact, location, link, skill, project, experience, or education proposal saves the edited value rather than the original extraction.
- Accepting a location proposal persists both city and region to the reviewed profile and the base profile where those fields are represented.
- Rejecting a proposal leaves the corresponding existing profile data unchanged.
- Resume review remains non-persistent until the user chooses Save reviewed proposals, and the saved result survives reload.
- Synthetic regression coverage proves the mapping without storing personal resume values in source, fixtures, logs, or task descriptions.

## Out of scope
- New PDF extraction filters, decompression limits, or multi-column reading-order work.
- Browser extension field detection, navigation handling, or session progress.
- Automatic approval, server sync, or application submission.

## Steps
1. **Make proposal values authoritative** — Update the resume approval mapping so accepted and edited proposals drive every saved contact field and structured collection entry, including location, links, skills, projects, experience, and education, while retaining provenance and excluding rejected proposals.
2. **Keep cockpit state aligned** — Ensure the approved assist profile and the existing base profile receive only the accepted contact changes, with no writes during preview and no accidental replacement of unrelated saved values.
3. **Add regression coverage** — Exercise accepted, edited, rejected, and location proposals with synthetic data at the library and cockpit layers, including persistence after reload and the no-accepted-proposals case.
